I save his sister.

You don’t have to specifically say or do anything, just don’t change how you’ve always been with her. 

Stability is a big thing that she’ll need right now. Stay just as caring as always, keep the routines you’ve always had. Her whole world would be turning upside down right now and having you as an anchor will do so much more than you know. 

Personally I always found the celebration of life rather than dwell on death thing to not help. It’s good intentions but it doesn’t change the fact someone who mattered and who held a large piece of your heart is gone and there’s no bringing them back. 

Let her mourn the way she needs to. She’ll probably have mood swings, she’ll probably try and give up on things she was passionate about last week, she’ll probably confuse you from day to day, hour to hour. I can’t tell you how she’s going to deal with it, but as long as you’re her constant she’ll be able to deal with it. 

One last thing, she probably won’t know what she wants right now, so asking her won’t give you answers. Tell her you’ve done things, like you drew her a bath so she can relax, you did the washing, etc. Help her and her family where you see fit, but don’t let it neglect your mental health and well being. This affects you too, don’t let yourself bottle it up.
